verdict.rationale: Twenty's docs claim a developer-first API (REST+GraphQL) with a Metadata API to programmatically create objects, fields, and relations, batch operations, webhooks, and an interactive playground — suggesting broad parity between UI and API capabilities, and custom objects get 'the same first-class treatment' including API endpoints, views, permissions, and workflow triggers. However, real-world corroboration is thin: one hands-on report notes the REST API 'worked ok' but the product was 'pretty alpha-version' with issues, and there's no explicit evidence that UI-built workflows, dashboards, or view configuration are fully API-manageable (only schema/data operations are clearly documented as API-parity). missing for 10: evidence that workflow/dashboard/view configuration (not just object/field schema and CRUD) is fully API-accessible, and stronger independent verification beyond one alpha-stage community report.
